sections.heading: What is an Abstract Class in Java?

content.text: An abstract class is a class that cannot be instantiated and may contain abstract methods (methods without implementation). It serves as a blueprint for other classes.

items: To define common behavior and structure while leaving specific implementations to subclasses.
To prevent instantiation of incomplete classes.
Useful when shared functionality should exist but individual behavior varies per subclass.
If a class has at least one abstract method, the class must be declared abstract.
Subclasses must implement all abstract methods, or else the subclass must also be declared abstract.

sections.heading: Scenario: Bank Branch Account Opening Process

items: Check for a minimum deposit of Rs 1000

content.text: Each branch has custom validation rules, so these need to be implemented by subclasses.

sections.heading: Best Practices for Using Abstract Classes

items: Use abstract classes to model template behaviors shared by multiple classes.
Avoid blank implementations in normal classes—enforce method implementation via abstract methods.
Define concrete methods for shared logic (e.g., openAccount()).
Use abstract classes when you want to:
Use abstract classes when behavior needs to be enforced but flexible per subclass.
Prevent instantiation of incomplete or base classes.
Helps in code reuse and enforcing custom rules per branch (or other subclass types).
